name: Posidonia oceanica meadows of Catalonia (Costa Brava)
description: Posidonia oceanica meadows of the Catalan coast, most of them on the Costa Brava: 10 agents, the meadow itself a keystone foundation species; the unit is the hectare and the reference resource is the regional stock (4,582 ha) unless the user enters the meadow a project affects. Every agent carries euros under any input: the service ledger books each final ecosystem service once, to one agent (the food the meadow's primary production supports, net of the commercial catch (production function, on every hectare), coastal protection, water purification, fisheries split between fish and invertebrates, bioindicator use split with the epiphytes, knowledge, recreational diving on the meadow (only near dive sites: --dive-site-share, at a stated diving intensity: --dive-intensity) and on the coralligenous, non-use values of megafauna and seabirds). Small losses are priced linearly (damage model area_loss). Carbon is valued by gaia.carbon. Sources: docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md; derivations: gaia/cases/definitions/CASE_NOTES.md.

resource.name: Posidonia oceanica meadows of Catalonia (Costa Brava)

area_ha.source: Generalitat de Catalunya, Mapa d'hàbitats marins de Catalunya (presented 29 May 2025; Hipermapa): P. oceanica meadows 4,582 ha, 2.4% of ~190,000 ha mapped to 50 m depth, as reported by Ara (29 May 2025, https://en.ara.cat/society/from-portbou-to-alcanar-this-is-the-catalan-seabed_1_5395705.html)
area_ha.note: The default reference resource: the whole Catalan stock (Portbou to Alcanar). A user assessing one project replaces it with the specific meadow the project affects (--area-ha N [--resource-name NAME], or resource.total_units/area_ha and resource.name in a copy of this file); the reference sets the depletion fraction, which matters once a project passes the safe threshold. The Costa Brava holds much of it (Cap de Creus) but the map's breakdown by coast was not available to this review, nor the dataset itself (the Govern's press-release PDF returned HTTP 403). The former 5,000 ha exceeded the whole Catalan stock.

unit_value.note: Project-specific input: the private gain per hectare of meadow destroyed (one-off), which the user sets with --unit-value for the project assessed. 2,500 is the former owner specification, kept as an illustration; no source can make it general.

safe_threshold_ratio.note: No ecological or regulatory source supports a 'safe' loss of 20% of a priority habitat (Habitats Directive 1120*): the value is the former owner specification. Under the case's area_loss damage model (Step 8c.3) it is the depletion of the reference resource beyond which the REMAINING meadow starts to degrade; below it each hectare lost costs exactly its average per-hectare value (linear benefit transfer). Monte Carlo range 0.1-0.3, uniform (judgement).

agent[*].dependency_weight.note: Owner-specified shares of ecosystem health (weights / 0.91 after the Blue Carbon agent was removed); no source. They set the health index and, with each agent's value, its € at full damage (weight × value = the sourced €/ha/yr service value).

edge[*].strength.note: Hand-set cascade strengths. The links themselves are documented (e.g. meadow -> wave attenuation: Infantes et al. 2012, MEPS 456:63-72, doi:10.3354/meps09754; seagrass -> fisheries: Jackson et al. 2015), their strengths are not. Monte Carlo range: ×0.5 to ×1.5 (judgement; wider ranges breach the in-degree cap).

steepness.note: Degradation of the remaining meadow past the safe threshold (damage model area_loss, Step 8c.3): zero up to the threshold, then a logistic with its inflection 15% into the post-threshold span (32% loss at the default threshold), the same curve for every agent. The damage of each agent is D + (1 - D) x degradation, so its slope at small losses is exactly 1 (each hectare lost costs its average value) and the curve shapes only the threshold behaviour. No Posidonia study relates the fraction of a meadow lost to the degradation of the rest, so the curve is not fitted (calibration regime B). Monte Carlo range 6-18, uniform (judgement).

agents.name: Posidonia Meadow
agents.description: The meadow itself, keystone foundation species and one of the most productive habitats of the sea; its own final services: the food its primary production (with its roots) supports (production function, net of the commercial catch booked to fish and invertebrates), on every hectare, and the underwater amenity divers enjoy (Zunino et al. 2020), only where the meadow is within reach of dive sites

annual_value_per_ha.source: Service ledger, production function (Step 8e.6): Pergent et al. (1994), doi:10.3354/meps106139; Duarte (1990), doi:10.3354/meps067201; Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043; Coll et al. (2008), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0003881; Francour (1997), doi:10.1111/j.1439-0485.1997.tb00434.x with FishBase; Pauly & Christensen (1995), doi:10.1038/374255a0; Zhou et al. (2012), doi:10.1139/f2012-060; Generalitat de Catalunya fisheries statistics (dataset ge3m-4jgm); roots: Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043, and Cebrián et al. (1997), doi:10.3354/meps155029; transfer efficiency: Sánchez-Zulueta et al. (2023), doi:10.3389/fmars.2023.1166674; depth function (Step 8g.1): Pergent et al. (1994), doi:10.3354/meps106139, Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043, and Cebrián et al. (1997), doi:10.3354/meps155029 (production by depth), Gobert et al. (2009), doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2009.06.012, and Generalitat de Catalunya (2004) (depth limits, mean depth); see production_function
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8e.6, 8f.1, 8f.2, 8g.1, 8g.2, 8g.4; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2b): the meadow's own value on EVERY hectare, whatever the diving: the food its primary production supports, 312.49 EUR/ha/yr gross (net primary production of the plant from its depth function at the regional mean depth, 15 m: 318 g DW = 107 g C/m2/yr, 81.1% not buried (shoots only, Step 8g.4); of its roots, 6.95 g C/m2/yr, 4% not buried: 868 kg C/ha/yr into the food web → 14.3% transfer per trophic level (Western Mediterranean food-web models) to trophic level 3.1 → x9 wet weight → 46.5% sustainable catch → EUR 5.11/kg), net of the 35 EUR/ha/yr of commercial catch already booked to Fish Populations and Marine Invertebrates: 277.49 EUR/ha/yr. The leaf epiphytes' food (52.33 EUR/ha/yr since Step 8h.1; 82.20 before) is the Epiphytes & Algae agent's since Step 8g.2. Weight x value = that net service. No site share or --dive-intensity scales it, so the meadow never falls to EUR 0 (PROJECT_DEFINITION.md, Core Valuation Principles); --depth-m sets the depth (Step 8g.1). Range: the chain at every link's least and most favourable end at once (3.83-1,525.48 EUR/ha/yr), divided by the weight: the hard bounds of any draw. The Monte Carlo does not sample this value as one aggregate: it samples each link of the production function, and the three hyperparameters of the depth function, from their own distributions and recomputes the chain in every draw (Step 8f.3; net P5 / P50 / P95 118 / 254 / 528 EUR/ha/yr, 1,000 draws, seed 20261012).

keystone_threshold.note: Health below which the meadow's outgoing edges double; hand-set, no source. Monte Carlo range 0.15-0.45, uniform (judgement).

site_share.source: European Environment Agency, Natura 2000 Standard Data Forms, habitat 1120* (Posidonia beds) cover in ha, forms last updated December 2014, via the EEA Natura 2000 service (https://bio.discomap.eea.europa.eu/arcgis/rest/services/Bio/Natura2000_Dyna_WM/MapServer/13, queried 12 October 2026; site pages https://natura2000.eea.europa.eu/Natura2000/SDF.aspx?site=ES5120007 etc.): Cap de Creus (ES5120007) 64.14 ha, El Montgrí-Les Medes-El Baix Ter (ES5120016) 10.75 ha, Litoral del Baix Empordà (ES5120015) 24.10 ha, Massís de les Cadiretes (ES5120013) 42.36 ha, L'Albera (ES5120014) 1.00 ha: 142.35 ha in the coastal Natura 2000 sites of the Costa Brava (Girona coast); cross-check: the Medes Islands meadow covers 8.8 ha (Romero, Pérez & Renom 2001, Seguimiento de la pradera de Posidonia oceanica de las islas Medes, Ejercicio 2001, Universitat de Barcelona, http://hdl.handle.net/2445/25506); regional stock 4,582 ha (resource.area_ha)
site_share.note: The share of the affected meadow within reach of dive sites, where the meadow's diving value applies (Step 8d.4). A PROJECT INPUT: the user states it with --dive-site-share (1 for a project at a dive site, 0 far from any; recorded as user-supplied). The default is the regional share: 142.35 ha near dive sites / 4,582 ha, the expected share for a meadow of unknown location. The 142.35 ha are a proxy, flagged: the P. oceanica cover inside the coastal Natura 2000 sites of the Costa Brava, which hold its best-known dive sites (Medes Islands, Cap de Creus; dive sites elsewhere in these sites assumed, not verified); a site boundary is not the reach of a dive site, and the 2014 forms and the 2025 regional map differ in date and method. Held fixed in the Monte Carlo ("distribution": "fixed").

site_value_per_ha.source: Zunino, Melaku Canu, Marangon & Troiano (2020), Frontiers in Marine Science 6:823, doi:10.3389/fmars.2019.00823: choice experiment with 221 Italian scuba divers (2016-17); a total loss of P. oceanica cover lowers the willingness to pay for a dive by about EUR 34 (MNL, Table 3: -34.71); about 60,000 dives a year at the Medes Islands: Ràdio Capital de l'Empordà (26 May 2026, reporting the Parc Natural del Montgrí, les Illes Medes i el Baix Ter / SUBMON study: 'prop de 60.000 immersions anuals'); the former annual cap was 60,000 and the 2015 plan raised it to almost 77,000 (Ara, 19 June 2015); meadow within reach of dive sites: 142.35 ha, the P. oceanica cover of the Costa Brava's coastal Natura 2000 sites (EEA Natura 2000 Standard Data Forms, see site_restricted.share)
site_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; restricted to dive sites in Step 8d.4; site_value_per_ha since Step 8e.6; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): recreational diving amenity of the meadow, PER HECTARE OF MEADOW WITHIN REACH OF DIVE SITES, on top of the meadow's value on every hectare (annual_value_per_ha): 14,630.14 EUR/ha/yr = EUR 34.71 per dive x 60,000 Medes dives a year / 142.35 ha of meadow near Costa Brava dive sites. A run multiplies it by site_share, the share of the affected meadow near dive sites: the regional default 142.35 / 4,582 = 0.0311 gives the regional average, 454.52 EUR/ha/yr (the former value); a project states its own (--dive-site-share: 1 at a dive site, 0 far from any). The value is stated at the Costa Brava's average diving intensity, 60,000 / 142.35 = 421.5 dives per hectare of meadow near dive sites per year (site_intensity); a project can state the intensity at its meadow (--dive-intensity none/low/medium/high, Step 8e.2), which scales it by level / 421.5. Unit-value benefit transfer of a per-dive WTP from Italian to Catalan divers (no income adjustment); it assumes every Medes dive includes meadow (an upper bias) and counts no dives at the other Costa Brava sites, whose numbers were not found (a lower bias). Range 6,874-41,651 EUR/ha/yr near dive sites (214-1,294 at the regional share): EUR 18.12/dive (the 50%-loss value, i.e. half the dives over meadow) x 54,000 dives to EUR 77/dive (latent class 1, total loss) x 77,000 dives (the plan's cap), over 142.35 ha; the uncertainty of the 142.35 ha is not sampled (at the regional share it cancels out). Weight x value = the service near dive sites.

site_intensity.source: about 60,000 dives a year at the Medes Islands (Ràdio Capital de l'Empordà, 26 May 2026, reporting the Parc Natural del Montgrí, les Illes Medes i el Baix Ter / SUBMON study) / 142.35 ha of P. oceanica within reach of the Costa Brava's dive sites (EEA Natura 2000 Standard Data Forms, see site_share)
site_intensity.note: The diving intensity at which the meadow's near-site value is stated (Step 8e.2): 60,000 / 142.35 = 421.5 dives per hectare of meadow near dive sites per year, the Costa Brava average (only the Medes dives are counted, a lower bias). A PROJECT INPUT through the levels of site_intensity_levels: --dive-intensity {none,low,medium,high} scales the near-site value by level / 421.5 (none 0, low 66.2, medium 566.5, high 5,581 dives/ha/yr) and is recorded as user-supplied. Held fixed in the Monte Carlo ("distribution": "fixed"); the meadow's value keeps its own relative range at any level.

none.description: No diving at or near the affected meadow (no dive site within reach): the meadow's diving value is zero. Only this service is zeroed, never an agent: the meadow keeps its own value on every hectare (the food its primary production supports), the other agents keep theirs, and its carbon still costs money.

low.description: Light diving use, like the Banyuls-Cerbère marine reserve and the Côte Vermeille (France, next to Cap de Creus): about 14,000 dives a year over 211 ha of meadow, some 66 dives per hectare of meadow a year.
low.basis: low confidence, grey literature: Lloret (2006), 'Recerca i gestió a dos espais costaners i marins fronterers: Cervera-Banyuls i Cap de Creus', conference slides, Institució Catalana d'Història Natural (https://ichn.iec.cat/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/ponencia-J_Lloret-cap-de-Creus-ICHN-2006.pdf, slide 10: Banyuls-Cervera, 24 dive centres, 14,000 dives a year); meadow: 211.45 ha of P. oceanica (habitat 1120) in Natura 2000 site FR9101482 'Posidonies de la côte des Albères' (EEA Natura 2000 Standard Data Form); 14,000 / 211.45 = 66.2 dives/ha/yr

medium.description: Busy diving, like the Portofino marine protected area (Liguria), one of Europe's main diving destinations: up to 40,000 dives a year over 71 ha of meadow, some 566 dives per hectare of meadow a year, close to the Costa Brava average (421, the default).
medium.basis: sourced (abstract): Betti et al. (2023), Aquatic Conservation: Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems 33(2):191-201, doi:10.1002/aqc.3918: Portofino MPA, 'up to 40,000 dives per year concentrated along 6.5 km of coast'; meadow: 70.61 ha of P. oceanica (habitat 1120) in Natura 2000 site IT1332674 'Fondali Monte Portofino' (EEA Natura 2000 Standard Data Form); 40,000 / 70.61 = 566.5 dives/ha/yr; 'up to' makes it an upper figure for Portofino

high.description: Intense diving, like the Medes Islands (L'Estartit), the most dived site of the Costa Brava: about 60,000 dives a year over 10.75 ha of meadow, some 5,600 dives per hectare of meadow a year. Only a small meadow at a heavily dived site reaches this; a larger affected meadow should state the share near the dive site (--dive-site-share).
high.basis: sourced, press report: about 60,000 dives a year at the Medes Islands (Ràdio Capital de l'Empordà, 26 May 2026, reporting the Parc Natural del Montgrí, les Illes Medes i el Baix Ter / SUBMON study); meadow: 10.75 ha of P. oceanica (habitat 1120) in Natura 2000 site ES5120016 'El Montgrí-Les Medes-El Baix Ter' (EEA Natura 2000 Standard Data Form); 60,000 / 10.75 = 5,581 dives/ha/yr (6,818 over the 8.8 ha Medes Islands meadow of Romero, Pérez & Renom 2001)

agents.name: Coralligenous & Red Coral
agents.description: Coralligenous reefs next to the meadow, smothered when it is lost (sedimentation); its own final service: recreational diving on coralligenous (Rodrigues et al. 2016, Medes Islands)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Rodrigues, van den Bergh, Loureiro, Nunes & Rossi (2016), Environmental and Resource Economics 63:289-311, doi:10.1007/s10640-015-9935-8: choice experiment with scuba divers at the Medes Islands MPA (Catalonia); the local extinction of gorgonians, the emblem of the coralligenous, costs divers about EUR 60 per dive; about 60,000 dives a year at the Medes Islands: Ràdio Capital de l'Empordà (26 May 2026, reporting the Parc Natural del Montgrí, les Illes Medes i el Baix Ter / SUBMON study: 'prop de 60.000 immersions anuals'); the former annual cap was 60,000 and the 2015 plan raised it to almost 77,000 (Ara, 19 June 2015); ~190,000 ha of seabed mapped to 50 m (Generalitat 2025 marine habitat map, as reported by Ara, 29 May 2025; see resource.area_ha)
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): recreational diving on the coralligenous, 18.95 EUR/ha/yr = EUR 60 per dive x 60,000 Medes dives a year / 190,000 ha of mapped seabed. A Catalan primary study; the attribution to a hectare of meadow is the seascape rule used for every service of the wider seascape: the regional value spread evenly over the mapped seabed. PROVISIONAL: an attribution assumption, not a source (no study links coralligenous condition to the nearby meadow), accepted by the owner as provisional (Step 8d.3) until an area-weighted link to nearby reefs can be sourced. Range 9.5-43.8 EUR/ha/yr: half the attribution to EUR 108.01/dive (Zunino et al. 2020, total loss of coralligenous) x 77,000 dives.

agents.name: Epiphytes & Algae
agents.description: Epiphytic algae and plant community: primary production, food web base; owns the food its own production supports (production function, Step 8g.2) and the epiphyte share of the bioindicator service (PREI E/L metric)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Service ledger: production function (Step 8g.2): Champenois & Borges (2021), Limnology and Oceanography 66:2126-2140, doi:10.1002/lno.11724, from Bay (1984), doi:10.1016/0304-3770(84)90026-3, with the meadow's chain to the catch (see the ledger); bioindicator: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): use as bioindicator 1.5 EUR/ha/yr; share: Gobert et al. (2009), Marine Pollution Bulletin 58:1727-1733, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2009.06.012, PREI EQR' = (N density + N leaf surface + N(E/L) + N lower limit)/3.5 with N(E/L) = [1 - E/L] x 0.5
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2, 8g.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2, §2b): two final services. (1) Since Step 8g.2, the food its own primary production supports (the owner's answer to PR #10 question 2: moved from the meadow's production function, where the epiphytes were a producer since Step 8f.2): 22.8 g C/m2/yr measured at 10 m, 14.5 at the regional mean depth, 15 m, on the plant's depth curve (Step 8h.1; 82.20 EUR/ha/yr before, with the 10 m figure used at 15 m), none buried → the meadow's chain to the catch (14.3% transfer per level to trophic level 3.1, x9, 46.5% sustainable catch, EUR 5.11/kg) = 52.33 EUR/ha/yr, not net of anything (the commercial catch stays netted out of the meadow's chain). (2) The epiphyte share of the bioindicator service, moved from Human Communities (total unchanged): 1.5 x 0.5/3.5 = 0.2143 EUR/ha/yr, the weight of the epiphyte/leaf biomass metric in the PREI index used to monitor P. oceanica; monitoring information, a cultural service, so it does not overlap the food. Weight x value = 52.55 EUR/ha/yr. Range: the food chain at every link's least and most favourable end and the depth function's shape (4.36-320.62) plus the bioindicator share, divided by the weight; the Monte Carlo does not sample this value as one aggregate: it samples the production function's links (the links shared with the meadow's chain drawn once for both) and recomputes it in every draw.

agents.name: Marine Invertebrates
agents.description: Sponges, urchins, octopus, lobsters, shellfish: grazers and filter feeders; owns the invertebrate share of the commercial fisheries contribution (sea urchin, cuttlefish)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): fishery contribution 27-35 EUR/ha/yr from 16 meadow-associated species sold at the Sète auction, two of them invertebrates (Paracentrotus lividus, Sepia officinalis), §3.2.4
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): the invertebrate share of the fisheries service, moved from Fish Populations (total unchanged): 35 x 2/16 = 4.375 EUR/ha/yr, by species count (2 of Campagne et al.'s 16 species; equal value per species is an assumption). Range 3.4-18.8 EUR/ha/yr: 27 x 2/16 to 74 x 0.254, the cephalopod and other-invertebrate share of Catalan white-fish, cephalopod and other-invertebrate first-sale value in 2014 (Generalitat, Estadístiques de pesca per grups biològics, dataset ge3m-4jgm: EUR 13.65 M + 0.34 M against 41.06 M; a proxy, not meadow-specific).

agents.name: Fish Populations
agents.description: Fish nursery and feeding habitat: contribution to commercial fisheries, fish species (Campagne et al. 2015)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): fishery contribution 27-35 EUR/ha/yr (production function); upper end used
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): the fish share of the fisheries service, 35 x 14/16 = 30.625 EUR/ha/yr (14 of the 16 species are fish; the two invertebrates go to Marine Invertebrates). Range 23.6-64.8 EUR/ha/yr: (27 to 74) x 14/16. 74 is derived here, not published: Jackson et al. (2015, Conservation Biology 29:899-909, doi:10.1111/cobi.12436) attribute EUR 58-91 million/yr of Mediterranean commercial landings to seagrass; divided by the known P. oceanica area, 1,224,707 ha (Telesca et al. 2015, Scientific Reports 5:12505, doi:10.1038/srep12505), that is EUR 47-74/ha/yr (an overestimate per ha of P. oceanica).

agents.name: Marine Megafauna
agents.description: Dolphins, sea turtles: apex predators; their own final service: the non-use (existence) value of protecting charismatic marine megafauna (Börger et al. 2014, benefit transfer)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Börger, Hattam, Burdon, Atkins & Austen (2014), Ecological Economics 108:229-241, doi:10.1016/j.ecolecon.2014.10.006: choice experiment, UK households pay GBP 30.32/yr (mixed logit; 5-year tax) to protect porpoises, seals and seabirds on 50% of the UK Dogger Bank (GBP 24.02 on 25%); 2,989,357 households in Catalonia (Idescat, Households by size, 2021, from the INE Population and Housing Census); ~190,000 ha of seabed mapped to 50 m (Generalitat 2025 marine habitat map, as reported by Ara, 29 May 2025; see resource.area_ha); ECB euro reference rate, GBP per EUR, 2013 annual average 0.84926
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): non-use value of protecting marine mammals (dolphins) and, by extension, sea turtles, 30.18 EUR/ha/yr: the 5-year payment of GBP 30.32 annualised at the case's 2.3% (GBP 3.26/yr in perpetuity), converted at 0.84926 GBP/EUR (EUR 3.84), times 2,989,357 Catalan households (EUR 11.5 M/yr), spread over 190,000 ha of mapped seabed (the seascape rule, PROVISIONAL: an attribution assumption accepted by the owner as provisional, Step 8d.3) and split equally between Marine Megafauna and Seabirds, which Börger et al.'s attribute bundles. A unit-value benefit transfer from the UK (no income adjustment) of a protection scenario (50% of an area) read as the value at full damage: a lower bound in scope, an uncertain transfer. Range x0.33-x3 (judgement).

agents.name: Seabirds
agents.description: Seabirds that feed on meadow fish (Audouin's gull); their own final service: the non-use (existence) value of protecting seabirds (Börger et al. 2014, benefit transfer)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Börger, Hattam, Burdon, Atkins & Austen (2014), Ecological Economics 108:229-241, doi:10.1016/j.ecolecon.2014.10.006: choice experiment, UK households pay GBP 30.32/yr (mixed logit; 5-year tax) to protect porpoises, seals and seabirds on 50% of the UK Dogger Bank (GBP 24.02 on 25%); 2,989,357 households in Catalonia (Idescat, Households by size, 2021, from the INE Population and Housing Census); ~190,000 ha of seabed mapped to 50 m (Generalitat 2025 marine habitat map, as reported by Ara, 29 May 2025; see resource.area_ha); ECB euro reference rate, GBP per EUR, 2013 annual average 0.84926
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): non-use value of protecting seabirds (Audouin's gull, shags, shearwaters), 30.18 EUR/ha/yr: the 5-year payment of GBP 30.32 annualised at the case's 2.3% (GBP 3.26/yr in perpetuity), converted at 0.84926 GBP/EUR (EUR 3.84), times 2,989,357 Catalan households (EUR 11.5 M/yr), spread over 190,000 ha of mapped seabed (the seascape rule, PROVISIONAL: an attribution assumption accepted by the owner as provisional, Step 8d.3) and split equally between Marine Megafauna and Seabirds, which Börger et al.'s attribute bundles. A unit-value benefit transfer from the UK (no income adjustment) of a protection scenario (50% of an area) read as the value at full damage: a lower bound in scope, an uncertain transfer. Range x0.33-x3 (judgement).

agents.name: Coastal Protection
agents.description: Wave attenuation, beach-cast banquettes and matte stabilisation against coastal erosion (Campagne et al. 2015)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): protection from coastal erosion 188 EUR/ha/yr (damage cost avoided, Mediterranean scale, 2001 data inflated to 2014)
annual_value_per_ha.note: 188 EUR/ha/yr of service at full damage = weight × value (service ledger, Step 8c.2) (188 / 0.142857). A single estimate; it covers wave attenuation, beach-cast banquettes and matte sediment stabilisation (Campagne et al.'s three services). Its spread in the Monte Carlo (×/÷2) is a judgement.

agents.name: Water Quality
agents.description: Nutrient and contaminant retention: the wastewater-treatment service (Campagne et al. 2015)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): wastewater treatment 60 EUR/ha/yr (benefit transfer of the French water-protection tax, one third attributed to coastal systems after Costanza et al. 1997)
annual_value_per_ha.note: 60 EUR/ha/yr of service at full damage = weight × value (service ledger, Step 8c.2) (60 / 0.120879). A single, crude benefit-transfer estimate. Its spread in the Monte Carlo (×/÷2) is a judgement.

agents.name: Human Communities
agents.description: Cultural services: bioindicator use (leaf, shoot and lower-limit metrics) and knowledge (Campagne et al. 2015)

stored_carbon_tonnes.source: Label Bas-Carbone, 'Méthode de protection des herbiers de posidonie' (French Ministry of Ecological Transition, approved 21 March 2023, NOR ENER2305073S; https://aida.ineris.fr/sites/aida/files/2023-04/Dec20230321_1.pdf), §7: the carbon in the living leaves is 'négligeable comparé au carbone stocké et séquestré dans la matte'
stored_carbon_tonnes.note: Living biomass is not counted separately: the leaves are negligible next to the matte, and the living rhizomes and roots lie inside the top-metre matte stock counted in soil_carbon_tonnes (counting them here too would double count). No Posidonia leaf-biomass carbon figure was verified for this review.

annual_absorption_tonnes.source: Mazarrasa et al. (2017), Limnology and Oceanography 62:1436-1450, doi:10.1002/lno.10510: organic carbon burial 26 ± 6 g C/m2/yr in Balearic P. oceanica meadows since 1900 (210Pb-dated cores) = 0.26 t C/ha/yr × 44/12
annual_absorption_tonnes.note: S5 resolved: one long-term burial (sequestration) rate, from the nearest region with direct measurements. Range 0.28-3.09 tCO2/ha/yr: 7.7-84.4 g C/m2/yr, the depth range of mean sequestration in a large Corsican meadow (Pergent-Martini et al. 2021, Marine Environmental Research 165:105236, doi:10.1016/j.marenvres.2020.105236). The former value, 1.58 tCO2/ha/yr, was the IPCC (2013) Wetlands Supplement Table 4.12 seagrass factor (0.434 t C/ha/yr, 95% CI 0.2-0.7, from Mateo & Romero 1997 and Serrano et al. 2012), which applies to revegetated meadows; it lies inside the range.

soil_carbon_tonnes.source: Monnier et al. (2022), Science of the Total Environment 838:155864, doi:10.1016/j.scitotenv.2022.155864 (39 matte cores, eastern Corsica: 327 ± 150 t Corg/ha), adopted as the Tier 1 default for 1 m of matte by Label Bas-Carbone, 'Méthode de protection des herbiers de posidonie' (French Ministry of Ecological Transition, approved 21 March 2023, NOR ENER2305073S; https://aida.ineris.fr/sites/aida/files/2023-04/Dec20230321_1.pdf); × 44/12
soil_carbon_tonnes.note: Organic carbon in the top metre of matte (the depth IPCC and the Label Bas-Carbone method treat as exposed), not the whole matte, which can be several metres thick. Range 741-1,844 tCO2/ha: 20.2-50.3 kg Corg/m2 in the first metre of matte in Calvi Bay (Leduc et al. 2023, Marine Environmental Research 183:105847, doi:10.1016/j.marenvres.2022.105847). Corsican, not Catalan, measurements; for scale, the IPCC (2013) global Tier 1 seagrass soil stock is 108 t C/ha to 1 m (Table 4.11) and Balearic P. oceanica holds 6.1 ± 1.4 kg C/m2 in the top 30 cm alone (Mazarrasa et al. 2017).

soil_release_fraction.source: Pendleton et al. (2012), PLoS ONE 7:e43542, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0043542: 25-100% of near-surface (top-metre) carbon lost upon conversion, central estimate 63%
soil_release_fraction.note: A project input (--carbon-release-fraction): it depends on what the project does to the matte. Recommended values (docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §4): excavated or dredged (port basins, channels) 0.96, the IPCC (2013) Wetlands Supplement Tier 1 for 'excavation to enable port, harbour and marina construction' (the top-metre soil carbon emitted in the year of extraction, minus 4% refractory); left exposed in place (meadow killed by shading, turbidity, anchoring or scour) 0.25-1.0, central 0.63 (this value, Pendleton et al.'s global range); buried under fill (breakwaters, reclaimed land) no source was found: the anoxic matte may keep much of its carbon (inferred, not sourced). The Label Bas-Carbone method models anchoring damage as a gradual loss (10.7% of the top-metre carbon over 10 years, after Mateo et al. 2019). The dominant uncertainty of the carbon externality.

release_half_life_years.source: Pendleton et al. (2012), PLoS ONE 7:e43542, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0043542: at a converted site the rate of release 'likely follows a negative exponential curve with time', with 'a half-life on the order of 5-10 years' (their ref. 29, a cleared mangrove)
release_half_life_years.note: A project input (--carbon-release-half-life): the time profile of the release, valued year by year at the carbon price of that year and discounted. 10 years is the upper end of Pendleton et al.'s order of magnitude; seagrass evidence brackets it: the exposed share of Shark Bay's seagrass soil carbon was estimated released within three years of the 2010/11 die-off (Arias-Ortiz et al. 2018, Nature Climate Change 8:338-344, doi:10.1038/s41558-018-0096-y); soil stocks were 72% lower 50 years after a disturbance (Macreadie et al. 2015, Proc. R. Soc. B 282:20151537, doi:10.1098/rspb.2015.1537), i.e. a half-life of at most 27 years if the decay were exponential (inferred here); 4.8 of 6.4 kg Corg/m2 of the top 50 cm were lost under moorings deployed from the 1930s (Serrano et al. 2016, Sci. Rep. 6:23193, doi:10.1038/srep23193). Excavated matte: 0 (the IPCC emits it in the year of extraction). Range 0-27 years (judgement from these sources).

exposed.description: The meadow dies but its matte stays in place, uncovered (killed by shading, turbidity, anchoring or scour around the works): the dead matte is open to oxygen and erodes, so its carbon escapes gradually over years to decades.
exposed.basis: sourced: Pendleton et al. 2012, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0043542, 25-100% lost, central 63%, negative exponential with a half-life of the order of 5-10 years; the 10-year central half-life is inferred (docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §4)

excavated.description: The matte is dug out or dredged (port basins, access channels, marina docks): the carbon-rich soil is removed and broken up, so nearly all of its carbon is released in the year of the works.
excavated.basis: sourced: IPCC 2013 Wetlands Supplement, ch. 4, Tier 1 for 'excavation to enable port, harbour and marina construction': the top-metre soil carbon emitted in the year of extraction, minus 4% refractory

buried.description: The matte is covered by fill (breakwaters, reclaimed land, rock armour): it stays buried without oxygen, which probably preserves most of its carbon.
buried.basis: INFERRED, no source: the midpoint of the inferred 0-0.25 range for anoxic burial; the half-life is the exposed default, for want of a measurement

net_of: Commercial fisheries: meadow-associated invertebrates (sea urchin, cuttlefish)
service_ledger.method: production function: net primary production of the plant (from its depth function), and its roots → food web (not buried) → trophic transfer to the catch's trophic level → sustainable catch → first-sale price
service_ledger.source: Pergent et al. (1994), doi:10.3354/meps106139; Duarte (1990), doi:10.3354/meps067201; Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043; Coll et al. (2008), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0003881; Francour (1997), doi:10.1111/j.1439-0485.1997.tb00434.x with FishBase; Pauly & Christensen (1995), doi:10.1038/374255a0; Zhou et al. (2012), doi:10.1139/f2012-060; Generalitat de Catalunya fisheries statistics (dataset ge3m-4jgm); roots: Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043, and Cebrián et al. (1997), doi:10.3354/meps155029; transfer efficiency: Sánchez-Zulueta et al. (2023), doi:10.3389/fmars.2023.1166674; depth function (Step 8g.1): Pergent et al. (1994), doi:10.3354/meps106139, Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043, and Cebrián et al. (1997), doi:10.3354/meps155029 (production by depth), Gobert et al. (2009), doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2009.06.012, and Generalitat de Catalunya (2004) (depth limits, mean depth); see production_function
service_ledger.transfer: Mediterranean (Ischia, Medes Islands, Port-Cros) and global trophic parameters to Catalonia; Catalan first-sale prices, EUR 2014
service_ledger.note: Step 8e.6 (owner's instruction: where there is no willingness-to-pay evidence, value what people consume). The gross value is every fish and invertebrate the meadow's own production can support at a sustainable catch, wherever and by whomever it is caught (commercial, artisanal, recreational, after the fish leave the meadow); the prey in between are the trophic steps, not valued again. It is booked net of the commercial fisheries already in the ledger (Fish Populations, Marine Invertebrates: 35 EUR/ha/yr, Campagne et al. 2015), which keep their entries. Not counted twice with carbon: the chain uses only the production that is not buried, gaia.carbon values the buried part. Coastal protection values the leaves' physical role (banquettes), not their food. Producers (Step 8f.2): the plant (leaf blades, sheaths, rhizomes) and its roots; each feeds the food web only with the production that is not buried (roots: 4%, the rest goes to the matte). The epiphytes on its leaves were a third producer until Step 8g.2, which moved their food (EUR 82.20/ha/yr gross) to the Epiphytes & Algae agent's own production function (the owner's answer to PR #10 question 2); the commercial catch stays netted out of this chain, whose lowest value still exceeds it. Depth (Step 8g.1): the plant's production falls with depth as light fades (depth_production: 770 g DW/m2/yr at 5 m, 318 at 15 m, 115 at 25 m, zero at the depth limit, 40 m); it is taken at the regional mean depth, 15 m (an inferred mean: no area-by-depth source could be read; conservative, the function being convex), or at the project's depth (--depth-m), where the commercial catch subtracted scales with the plant's production (NPP at the project's depth / NPP at 15 m: the part of the regional catch that hectare's production supports). Any project depth is valued (Step 8g.7): a meadow that lives there proves its site's depth limit lies deeper, so the project's curve reaches zero at the regional depth limit conditioned on lying at least 2 m below the deepest depth given (depth_limit_margin), keeping P_ref and k. Share not buried (Step 8g.4, PR #10 question 4): 81.1%, the shoots' own (blades over blades + sheaths + rhizomes, Medes Islands), now that the roots are a separate producer (74%, the whole-plant figure, before). Range over the links' ranges, every link at its least or most favourable end at once and the depth function's shape searched over its ranges: gross 38.83-1,560.48, net 3.83-1,525.48 EUR/ha/yr. In the Monte Carlo each link (and each depth hyperparameter) is sampled on its own, from its own distribution (distribution, distribution_basis), and every draw recomputes gross - net_of (Step 8f.3): net P5 / P50 / P95 118 / 254 / 528 EUR/ha/yr; parsing requires the lowest value to exceed what it is net of, so no draw reaches EUR 0. The subtraction is the booked 35 EUR in every draw, not coupled to the fisheries values sampled in the same draw (the owner's decision, Step 8g.3, PR #10 question 3). Transfer efficiency since Step 8f.1: 14.3%, the median of five Western Mediterranean food-web models (11.8%, the global median, before). Conservative: no microphytobenthos or other algae, first-sale (not retail) prices, only the sustainable share of production.

carbon_fraction.label: carbon content of seagrass dry weight
carbon_fraction.source: Duarte (1990), Marine Ecology Progress Series 67:201-207, doi:10.3354/meps067201 (abstract): mean carbon content of seagrass leaves 33.6 ± 0.31% of dry weight (27 species, 30 locations); applied to sheaths and rhizomes as well
carbon_fraction.distribution_basis: Duarte (1990): 33.6 ± 0.31% (SE) over 27 species; an uncertainty of under 1% is not sampled

food_web_share.label: share of the plant's production (blades, sheaths, rhizomes; its roots are a separate producer) eaten, decomposed or exported (to beaches and deep water) rather than buried in the matte
food_web_share.source: Mateo & Romero (1997), Marine Ecology Progress Series 151:43-53, doi:10.3354/meps151043 (full text, archived copy of the publisher's PDF, Table 3, carbon, Medes Islands, Catalonia): the leaf blades are not buried, the sheaths and rhizomes go to the matte: blades 252 of 252 + 51 + 15 g C/m2/yr at 5 m = 79.2% not buried, 87 of 87 + 12 + 6 at 13 m = 82.9%; value = their mean, 81.1% (shoot-only: the roots are a separate producer since Step 8f.2; the whole-plant figure in the abstract, 26% buried so 74% not, counts the roots; from Table 5's whole-plant burial, 84 and 24 g C, less the roots, 10 and 5, it would be 76.7% and 81.9%). Range: 71%, Pergent et al. (1994, doi:10.3354/meps106139, abstract and full text: production of blades, sheaths and rhizomes, no roots; 42% degraded in place, 29% exported, 29% buried in the matte); 83.2%, Cebrián, Duarte, Marbà & Enríquez (1997), Marine Ecology Progress Series 155:29-44, doi:10.3354/meps155029 (abstract and full text: 16.8% of P. oceanica production, blades, sheaths and rhizomes, roots not determined, neither consumed nor decomposed in its first year, Cala Jonquet, Catalonia). Mateo & Romero add that most of it reaches animals through the detritus and its microbes (48% lost as very fine particles, 17% respired), not directly: the transfer efficiency of the next link carries that loss
food_web_share.distribution_basis: Shoot-only estimates (Pergent et al. 1994, 71%; Mateo & Romero 1997, 79.2% at 5 m and 82.9% at 13 m; Cebrián et al. 1997, 83.2%): triangular with its mode at the Medes Islands mean, 81.1% (Step 8g.4, the owner's answer to PR #10 question 4; 74%, the whole-plant figure, before)

transfer_efficiency.label: trophic transfer efficiency per level (Western Mediterranean food-web models)
transfer_efficiency.source: Sánchez-Zulueta, Valls, Guijarro, Ángeles Torres, Ángeles Zapata, Coll, Corrales, Andonegi, Díaz-Valdés, Massutí & Ordines (2023), Frontiers in Marine Science 10:1166674, doi:10.3389/fmars.2023.1166674 (full text read), Table 3, mean transfer efficiency of five Western Mediterranean Ecopath models: Balearic Islands 21.80%, Gulf of Alicante 13.9% (García-Rodríguez et al. 2021), South Catalan Sea 12.2% (Coll et al. 2006, doi:10.1016/j.jmarsys.2005.09.001), north-western Mediterranean 14.3% (Corrales et al. 2015, doi:10.1016/j.jmarsys.2015.03.006, the model that covers the Catalan coast), Gulf of Lions 19.7% (Banaru et al. 2013); value = their median, 14.3% (= the north-western Mediterranean model), range = their minimum and maximum (12.2-21.8%). The original model papers were not read (closed access); their values are as tabulated in the 2023 comparison. Cross-check: Coll, Libralato, Tudela, Palomera & Pranovi (2008), PLoS ONE 3:e3881, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0003881 (full text read), Methods (e) 'Data sources': temperate and high-latitude ecosystem models mean 14.25% (sd 5.95, median 13.7, n = 39); all 91 models median 11.8%. No P. oceanica-specific Ecopath efficiency could be read (Valls et al. 2012 and Prato et al. 2014, Port-Cros, behind bot checks)
transfer_efficiency.distribution_basis: Five model values (12.2-21.8%), right-skewed (mean 16.4%, median 14.3%): triangular with its mode at the median, mean 16.1%; the Balearic upper end is kept (the owner's decision, Step 8g.3, PR #10 question 5)

catch_trophic_level.label: mean trophic level of the catch
catch_trophic_level.source: Francour (1997), Marine Ecology 18:157-173, doi:10.1111/j.1439-0485.1997.tb00434.x (abstract): P. oceanica fish assemblages at Port-Cros dominated by Symphodus ocellatus, S. tinca, Diplodus annularis and Sarpa salpa; FishBase trophic levels from diet studies (fishbase.se, queried 13 October 2026) 3.5, 3.3, 3.6, 2.0: mean 3.1. sustainable_catch_share.label: share of the production that can be caught sustainably (exploitation rate at maximum sustainable yield)

depth_production.description: Net primary production of P. oceanica (blades, sheaths and rhizomes) by depth: light falls exponentially with depth (Beer-Lambert) and, below light saturation, so does photosynthesis, while respiration does not, so production reaches zero at the depth limit. A seagrass (an angiosperm); other marine primary producers use the same shape with their own hyperparameters

npp_at_reference_depth.label: net primary production of the plant (blades, sheaths, rhizomes) at the reference depth, 10 m
npp_at_reference_depth.source: Fitted to 6 measurements of blades + sheaths + rhizomes (see data): Cebrián et al. (1997), doi:10.3354/meps155029, Cala Jonquet 4 m; Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043, Medes Islands 5 and 13 m; Pergent et al. (1994), doi:10.3354/meps106139, Ischia 5, 10 and 20 m; by scripts/fit_depth_production.py (see fit)
npp_at_reference_depth.distribution_basis: Site-to-site variation around the curve is multiplicative: lognormal with its median at the fit and the 95% prediction interval of a site's production at 10 m as its central 95% (×/÷ exp(1.96 × 0.236): the residual and the fit's standard error together), truncated at the range ends

decline_rate.label: decline rate of production with depth (the light attenuation coefficient Kd where production is light-limited)

decline_rate.distribution_basis: The fit ± 1.96 standard errors, triangular with its mode at the fit

depth_limit.label: depth limit: the depth at which the plant's net production reaches zero
depth_limit.source: Generalitat de Catalunya, Departament de Medi Ambient i Habitatge (2004), Els prats submarins de Posidònia: guia pedagògica, quadern del professorat (scientific supervision J. Romero), http://www.gencat.cat/mediamb/publicacions/monografies/prats_posidonia_guia_professorat.pdf (read): Catalan meadows grow on well-lit bottoms between 0 and 25 m and 'atenyen els 40 metres en aigües molt transparents de les Balears, Malta, Còrsega'; their lower limit is 'molt regular, situat al voltant dels 30 metres', set mainly by light. Gobert, Sartoretto, Rico-Raimondino, Andral, Chery, Lejeune & Boissery (2009), Marine Pollution Bulletin 58:1727-1733, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2009.06.012 (author copy on Archimer, read): meadows 'between the surface and 44 m depth in the clearest waters'; stable lower limits 37 ± 1 m in Corsica and 25 ± 3 m in Provence (reference values 41 and 34 m). Value 40 m: where meadows end in very transparent waters (the plant still grows there, so its production reaches zero no shallower); low end 30 m: the Catalan meadows' regular lower limit; high end 44 m: the deepest meadows
depth_limit.distribution_basis: The depths are read; that the plant's production reaches zero at them is an inference (meadows end where light no longer sustains them): triangular, mode 40 m, between the Catalan lower limit (30 m) and the deepest meadows (44 m)

depth_limit_margin.label: least depth between a meadow valued at a project depth and its site's depth limit (where the plant's net production reaches zero)
depth_limit_margin.source: Mateo & Romero (1997), Marine Ecology Progress Series 151:43-53, doi:10.3354/meps151043 (full text, archived copy of the publisher's PDF, Material and methods, 'Study site'): the Medes Islands meadow extends 'from 3 to 15 m depth'; its deeper station, at 13 m, is 'close to the lower limit, where the meadow is much sparser with ca 100 shoots m-2', and still produced 271 g DW/m2/yr (Table 3; see data). So a living meadow 2 m above its lower limit is still productive: the closest any of the measurements fitted lies to its own meadow's limit. Value: 2 m, the least distance at which a meadow is known to live and produce above its limit; that the site's depth limit (zero net production) lies at least this far below a meadow is an inference
depth_limit_margin.distribution_basis: A conditioning margin, not an uncertain quantity of the valuation: not sampled (Step 8g.7)

regional_depth.source: Generalitat de Catalunya (2004), Els prats submarins de Posidònia: guia pedagògica, quadern del professorat (read): 'la praderia mitjana de la costa catalana a 15 metres' (the average meadow of the Catalan coast, at 15 m, in a worked exercise), and Catalan meadows between the surface and their lower limit at about 30 m (midpoint 15 m); 15 m is also the standard monitoring depth of the PREI index (Gobert et al. 2009, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2009.06.012, author copy, read)
regional_depth.note: A mean depth, not an area-weighted distribution: no source giving the Catalan meadow's area by depth could be read (the Generalitat's 2025 marine habitat map and its bathymetry are not downloadable; the EMODnet Seabed Habitats seagrass layer did not answer). The function is convex and declining, so the production at the mean depth is below the mean production over the depths around it (e.g. 318 at 15 m against 413 g DW/m2/yr averaged evenly over 0-30 m): conservative

depth_production.fit: Fitted by scripts/fit_depth_production.py: least squares on ln(production) of the 6 measurements in 'data' (3 sites, 3 studies, 4-20 m; depths as the authors give them), with z_ref = 10 m (near the data's mean depth, so the two fitted hyperparameters are almost uncorrelated) and z_max fixed at its literature value (the data do not reach it). P_ref = 498.8 g DW/m2/yr (standard error of ln P_ref 0.090), k = 0.0803/m (standard error 0.0191), correlation -0.12; residual standard deviation of ln(production) 0.218 (sites scatter about ×/÷ 1.24 around the curve). Medes (a turbid site whose meadow ends at 15 m) lies below the curve at 13 m, Cala Jonquet (sampled at its densest depth) above it at 4 m. Cross-check: at Port Lligat (Cap de Creus), where the meadow reaches 15.6 m, leaf production per m2 'declined 5- to 6-fold with depth' (Olesen, Enríquez, Duarte & Sand-Jensen 2002, Marine Ecology Progress Series 236:89-97, doi:10.3354/meps236089, full text; no values tabulated), steeper than the regional curve, as expected where the meadow ends shallower. Not used: Pergent-Martini, Rico-Raimondino & Pergent (1994), Marine Biology 120:9-15, doi:10.1007/BF00381936, production at 22 Mediterranean sites by depth (closed access; only its metadata on Crossref and a search-engine summary were seen)

producers.name: roots
producers.description: the plant's roots: produced in the sediment and almost all buried in the matte; only the part decomposed within a year reaches the food web

npp_dry_weight.label: root production of the plant
npp_dry_weight.source: Mateo & Romero (1997), Marine Ecology Progress Series 151:43-53, doi:10.3354/meps151043 (full text, Table 3, by lepidochronology): roots 23 g dry weight/m2/yr at 5 m and 11 at 13 m, Medes Islands (Catalonia); value = their mean, range = the two depths. Cebrián et al. (1997, doi:10.3354/meps155029, Table 1) did not determine P. oceanica root production at Cala Jonquet (their method 'was not adequate for P. oceanica')
npp_dry_weight.distribution_basis: Two depths, no reason to prefer either: uniform between them

carbon_fraction.label: carbon content of living roots
carbon_fraction.source: Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043 (full text, Table 4): living roots 40.9% carbon of dry weight at both 5 and 13 m, Medes Islands
carbon_fraction.distribution_basis: The same 40.9% at both depths: not sampled

food_web_share.label: share of root production decomposed within its first year rather than buried in the matte
food_web_share.source: Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043 (full text) assume all root and rhizome production is stored in the sediment, where decay is 'practically negligible at least on a mid-term basis (i.e. decades)'. Cebrián et al. (1997), doi:10.3354/meps155029 (full text), use 0.00015 per day for the decay of all belowground parts of P. oceanica, from Mateo (1995, PhD thesis, Universitat de Barcelona; not read): 1 - exp(-0.00015 x 365) = 5.3% of a year's roots decomposed within the year if produced at its start, 2.7% if produced evenly over it; value = the midpoint, 4%. The other 95-97% is buried, and gaia.carbon values the burial (decision D3: the chain uses only what is not buried)
food_web_share.distribution_basis: Between the two bounding assumptions on when the roots are produced (evenly over the year, or at its start): uniform

comparison.note: Gross production of whole communities, the comparable measure across these sources. The meadow's chain above starts from the net production of the plant and its roots (114 g C/m²/yr at the regional mean depth, Steps 8f.2 and 8g.1), the epiphytes' chain from the leaf epiphytes' 22.8 (Step 8g.2): 136 g C/m²/yr together, with no other algae and no microphytobenthos, which is not comparable with these gross figures. Per hectare, seagrass meadows fix carbon on the scale of coral reefs and intensively farmed land; the Corsican P. oceanica meadow, measured over 12 years, fixes about half the seagrass average and 15 times the bare sediment around it.

service_ledger.service: Food from the leaf epiphytes' primary production: fish and invertebrates it supports
service_ledger.method: production function: net primary production of the leaf epiphytes (from their depth function, the plant's shape) → food web (none buried) → trophic transfer to the catch's trophic level → sustainable catch → first-sale price
service_ledger.source: Champenois & Borges (2021), doi:10.1002/lno.11724, from Bay (1984), doi:10.1016/0304-3770(84)90026-3 (production); Tomas, Turon & Romero (2005), doi:10.3354/meps287115, and Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043 (not buried); the meadow's chain from the food web to the catch: Sánchez-Zulueta et al. (2023), doi:10.3389/fmars.2023.1166674; Francour (1997), doi:10.1111/j.1439-0485.1997.tb00434.x with FishBase; Pauly & Christensen (1995), doi:10.1038/374255a0; Zhou et al. (2012), doi:10.1139/f2012-060; Generalitat de Catalunya fisheries statistics (dataset ge3m-4jgm); depth (Step 8g.9): Lepoint, Havelange, Gobert & Bouquegneau (1999), doi:10.1023/A:1003557303904, and the plant's depth function; see production_function
service_ledger.transfer: Corsican epiphyte production and Mediterranean and global trophic parameters to Catalonia; Catalan first-sale prices, EUR 2014
service_ledger.note: Step 8g.2 (the owner's answer to PR #10 question 2): the food the epiphytes' production supports, moved from the Posidonia Meadow's production function (where it was a producer, Step 8f.2) to the agent that is the epiphytes, through the ledger: same producer, same links, the same EUR 82.20/ha/yr gross at the time, so the total was unchanged and nothing is counted twice. The links from the food web to the catch are the meadow's (one food web): the Monte Carlo draws each of them once for both chains. Not net of anything: the commercial catch (35 EUR/ha/yr) stays netted out of the meadow's chain, whose lowest value still exceeds it (parsing checks it). Not counted twice with the bioindicator entry of the same agent (monitoring information, a cultural service). Range over the links' ends and the depth function's shape: EUR 4.36-320.62/ha/yr. Conservative: no other algae or microphytobenthos, first-sale prices, the sustainable share only. Depth (Step 8g.9, the owner's review of #11, question 4): the epiphytes need light, so their production follows the plant's depth function (the same decline rate and depth limit, drawn once with the meadow's: one light field), anchored at the depth their annual production was measured, 10 m (Step 8h.1, the owner's decision; it was used as the 15 m value before, EUR 82.20): at the regional mean depth, 15 m, EUR 52.33 = the 10 m value x NPP_plant(15 m) / NPP_plant(10 m); at a project depth (--depth-m) the 10 m value x NPP_plant(depth) / NPP_plant(10 m), never EUR 0. The shape is inferred: no epiphyte production by depth could be read.

food_web_share.label: share of epiphyte production eaten, decomposed or exported rather than buried
food_web_share.source: Inferred: the epiphytes are grazed (sea urchins at 5 per m2 cut the epiphyte load by about 60%, fish by about 30%: Tomas, Turon & Romero 2005, Marine Ecology Progress Series 287:115-125, doi:10.3354/meps287115, abstract), they are not found in the leaf litter, 'probably because they detach soon after leaf abscission', and the matte stores roots, rhizomes and sheaths (Mateo & Romero 1997, doi:10.3354/meps151043, full text). Value: none buried. Lower end: buried like the whole plant, roots included (74% not buried, Mateo & Romero 1997's whole-plant figure, abstract)
food_web_share.distribution_basis: Probably none buried (the value, the mode); at worst buried like the plant (74%): triangular

transfer_efficiency.label: trophic transfer efficiency per level (Western Mediterranean food-web models)
transfer_efficiency.source: Sánchez-Zulueta, Valls, Guijarro, Ángeles Torres, Ángeles Zapata, Coll, Corrales, Andonegi, Díaz-Valdés, Massutí & Ordines (2023), Frontiers in Marine Science 10:1166674, doi:10.3389/fmars.2023.1166674 (full text read), Table 3, mean transfer efficiency of five Western Mediterranean Ecopath models: Balearic Islands 21.80%, Gulf of Alicante 13.9% (García-Rodríguez et al. 2021), South Catalan Sea 12.2% (Coll et al. 2006, doi:10.1016/j.jmarsys.2005.09.001), north-western Mediterranean 14.3% (Corrales et al. 2015, doi:10.1016/j.jmarsys.2015.03.006, the model that covers the Catalan coast), Gulf of Lions 19.7% (Banaru et al. 2013); value = their median, 14.3% (= the north-western Mediterranean model), range = their minimum and maximum (12.2-21.8%). The original model papers were not read (closed access); their values are as tabulated in the 2023 comparison. Cross-check: Coll, Libralato, Tudela, Palomera & Pranovi (2008), PLoS ONE 3:e3881, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0003881 (full text read), Methods (e) 'Data sources': temperate and high-latitude ecosystem models mean 14.25% (sd 5.95, median 13.7, n = 39); all 91 models median 11.8%. No P. oceanica-specific Ecopath efficiency could be read (Valls et al. 2012 and Prato et al. 2014, Port-Cros, behind bot checks)
transfer_efficiency.distribution_basis: Five model values (12.2-21.8%), right-skewed (mean 16.4%, median 14.3%): triangular with its mode at the median, mean 16.1%; the Balearic upper end is kept (the owner's decision, Step 8g.3, PR #10 question 5)

No epiphyte-specific relation with depth was found (inferred)

npp_at_reference_depth.label: net primary production of the leaf epiphytes at the reference depth, 10 m (where it was measured)
npp_at_reference_depth.source: The Corsican annual figure, anchored at its measured depth, 10 m (Step 8h.1, the owner's decision: like the plant's, the measured value sits at its measured depth on the depth curve, and the regional value is the curve at 15 m, 22.8 x NPP_plant(15 m) / NPP_plant(10 m) = 14.5 g C/m2/yr; until Step 8h.1 the 10 m figure was used as the 15 m value). Champenois & Borges (2021), Limnology and Oceanography 66:2126-2140, doi:10.1002/lno.11724 (full text, author copy on ORBi, Fig. 6, re-read for Step 8h.1): epiphytes 1.9 mol C/m2/yr, against 15.3 for the P. oceanica leaves and 0.5 below ground, in the figure's budget of 'a Posidonia oceanica seagrass meadow at 10 m depth' (Bay of Revellata, Corsica; the caption attributes the epiphytes' figure to Bay (1984) in the Bay of Revellata), from Bay (1984), Aquatic Botany 20:43-64, doi:10.1016/0304-3770(84)90026-3 (not read: closed access, no abstract on Crossref, Semantic Scholar or OpenAlex; metadata checked on Crossref; so the 10 m depth is the depth Champenois & Borges give the budget, not read in Bay's own text); x 12.011 g C/mol = 22.8 g C/m2/yr, 12% of the leaves' production. No Catalan or other Mediterranean annual figure was found. Range x/÷2, the default range of a low-confidence value (gaia.uncertainty), a judgement, not a source. For scale: epiphytic algae contribute 20-60% of seagrass meadow primary production across species (Marbà et al. 2006, as cited by Champenois & Borges 2021); on P. oceanica leaf sections in short laboratory incubations at Ischia, epiphytes gave 62% of net primary production at ambient pH (Berlinghof et al. 2022, Scientific Reports 12:6249, doi:10.1038/s41598-022-10154-7, full text), a rate on epiphyte-covered leaf parts, not an annual meadow figure
npp_at_reference_depth.distribution_basis: One site, a range of x/÷2 (a judgement): lognormal with its median at the value and the range as its central 95%, truncated at the range ends

decline_rate.label: decline rate of the epiphytes' production with depth: the plant's (the light attenuation the meadow's curve was fitted to)
decline_rate.source: Inferred: the epiphytes are algae that need light, and their biomass is 'mainly related to the substrate leaf availability' and 'decreases with increasing depth' (Lepoint, Havelange, Gobert & Bouquegneau 1999, Hydrobiologia 394:63-67, doi:10.1023/A:1003557303904, abstract on ORBi, Revellata Bay, the site of the epiphytes' production figure; no epiphyte production by depth is given), so their production follows the plant's depth function, the same light: the plant's decline rate, fitted as follows. Fitted to 6 measurements of blades + sheaths + rhizomes (see data): Cebrián et al. (1997), doi:10.3354/meps155029, Cala Jonquet 4 m; Mateo & Romero (1997), doi:10.3354/meps151043, Medes Islands 5 and 13 m; Pergent et al. (1994), doi:10.3354/meps106139, Ischia 5, 10 and 20 m; by scripts/fit_depth_production.py (see fit). For scale: diffuse light attenuation below 0.2/m at Port Lligat (Olesen et al. 2002, doi:10.3354/meps236089, full text)
decline_rate.distribution_basis: The fit ± 1.96 standard errors, triangular with its mode at the fit

depth_limit.label: depth limit of the epiphytes' production: the plant's (they live on its leaves)
depth_limit.source: Inferred: the epiphytes live on the plant's leaves, so they end where the meadow ends: the plant's depth limit. Generalitat de Catalunya, Departament de Medi Ambient i Habitatge (2004), Els prats submarins de Posidònia: guia pedagògica, quadern del professorat (scientific supervision J. Romero), http://www.gencat.cat/mediamb/publicacions/monografies/prats_posidonia_guia_professorat.pdf (read): Catalan meadows grow on well-lit bottoms between 0 and 25 m and 'atenyen els 40 metres en aigües molt transparents de les Balears, Malta, Còrsega'; their lower limit is 'molt regular, situat al voltant dels 30 metres', set mainly by light. Gobert, Sartoretto, Rico-Raimondino, Andral, Chery, Lejeune & Boissery (2009), Marine Pollution Bulletin 58:1727-1733, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2009.06.012 (author copy on Archimer, read): meadows 'between the surface and 44 m depth in the clearest waters'; stable lower limits 37 ± 1 m in Corsica and 25 ± 3 m in Provence (reference values 41 and 34 m). Value 40 m: where meadows end in very transparent waters (the plant still grows there, so its production reaches zero no shallower); low end 30 m: the Catalan meadows' regular lower limit; high end 44 m: the deepest meadows
depth_limit.distribution_basis: The depths are read; that the plant's production reaches zero at them is an inference (meadows end where light no longer sustains them): triangular, mode 40 m, between the Catalan lower limit (30 m) and the deepest meadows (44 m)

depth_limit_margin.label: least depth between a meadow valued at a project depth and its site's depth limit (where the plant's net production reaches zero)
depth_limit_margin.source: Mateo & Romero (1997), Marine Ecology Progress Series 151:43-53, doi:10.3354/meps151043 (full text, archived copy of the publisher's PDF, Material and methods, 'Study site'): the Medes Islands meadow extends 'from 3 to 15 m depth'; its deeper station, at 13 m, is 'close to the lower limit, where the meadow is much sparser with ca 100 shoots m-2', and still produced 271 g DW/m2/yr (Table 3; see data). So a living meadow 2 m above its lower limit is still productive: the closest any of the measurements fitted lies to its own meadow's limit. Value: 2 m, the least distance at which a meadow is known to live and produce above its limit; that the site's depth limit (zero net production) lies at least this far below a meadow is an inference
depth_limit_margin.distribution_basis: A conditioning margin, not an uncertain quantity of the valuation: not sampled (Step 8g.7)

regional_depth.source: The meadow's regional mean depth (see the Posidonia Meadow's depth_production): Generalitat de Catalunya (2004), 'la praderia mitjana de la costa catalana a 15 metres'
regional_depth.note: The epiphytes' production is valued where the meadow is (their substrate is its leaves): at the meadow's regional mean depth, 15 m (14.5 g C/m2/yr on the curve anchored at 10 m), or at a project's depth

depth_production.fit: Not fitted: no production of P. oceanica leaf epiphytes by depth could be read (Lepoint et al. 1999, doi:10.1023/A:1003557303904, abstract: biomass decreases with depth at Revellata Bay, no rates). The shape is the plant's (scripts/fit_depth_production.py fits the meadow's), anchored at the one annual figure's depth, 10 m (Step 8h.1), so at any depth the epiphytes' production is 22.8 g C/m2/yr x NPP_plant(depth) / NPP_plant(10 m): 14.5 at the regional 15 m; the roots' production does not depend on depth

service_ledger.service: Recreational diving: meadow amenity near dive sites

run.report_note:
⚠  MARINE EXTERNALITY NOTE: the per-agent costs are ANNUAL (€/yr) — they
     recur every year the meadow is gone. P. oceanica grows centimetres a year;
     natural recolonisation leaves limited cover after a century (Kendrick et
     al. 2005). Every agent's value is a final service booked once in the
     case's service ledger, and no input brings an agent to €0; beach
     tourism and the meadow's own non-use value are still not valued.
     Sources: docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md.
json_notes: Marine externality costs are ANNUAL (€/yr): they recur every year the meadow is gone. P. oceanica rhizomes grow only centimetres a year and a model of natural recolonisation leaves limited cover after a century (Kendrick et al. 2005), so loss is effectively permanent on human timescales. The net social cost compares the one-off private gain with the present value of these annual losses and of the carbon released. Every agent's euro value is a final ecosystem service booked once in the case's service ledger (Step 8c.2), and no input brings an agent to €0: the meadow's own value is the food its primary production supports (a production function, Step 8e.6), on every hectare; beach tourism and the meadow's own non-use value are still not valued, so the services total remains a lower bound.
